notes:
- Nova is the page every install opens into: The redesigned Info page is now the default. A reader who has never chosen a title page, or who installs the app for the first time, opens the full-bleed artwork, cover-derived colours, score strip and progress card instead of the original card stack. Classic is not removed: it stays under Settings > Interface > App layout, and an install that already chose Classic keeps that choice.
- A palette that belongs to the artwork: The Nova page now derives a complete Material 3 scheme from the cover it is showing - primary for the entry capsule, a primary container behind the score strip, a secondary container behind progress, and tinted neutrals for the cards and the docked bar - instead of painting the whole page in one standing accent. Light and dark schemes are both generated from the same seed, so the page follows the reader's theme without the cover's text tones collapsing.
- Hold the progress bar to choose its style: Holding the progress card for about three seconds expands three styles directly beneath the bar, inside the same card: the original wave, a simple determinate bar, and a rocket route that ends at the moon. Each option previews itself at the current fraction. Choosing one applies it and collapses the row immediately; the rocket and the fill spring to a new position when progress changes, and the choice is remembered for every title on both the Nova and Classic Info pages. The count is still edited from My Entry; the row changes only how it is drawn.
- A title that reads over its own artwork: The Nova lockup's title and alternative spelling used to sit on bare key art with a rectangular shadow, which vanished over bright skies and white clothing. They now sit on a quiet rounded scrim whose light or dark tone is chosen against the cover, with matching ink and a hairline edge, so the name is readable at any font scale without hiding the picture.
- Nova's contrast and polish: The score strip, countdown, progress card and progress count now use matching on-container foregrounds instead of borrowing the page's surface text, and the shared cards use the cover-derived neutral ramp. The hero's title backing replaces the hard rectangular shadow that made the old treatment look like a grey box.
- A closer look at every title statistic: The score, popularity, favourites and episode-length figures now open a compact interactive detail drawer on tap or long-press. It uses AniList's score and list-status distributions, title rankings, favourite totals and synopsis when those fields are available; unavailable figures are labelled rather than guessed.
- The episode countdown stays present at release: The next-episode line now reaches an explicit 'now' state at the scheduled release moment instead of disappearing at zero. It clears after a short grace period when AniList has not yet supplied a newer schedule.
- The artwork returns with the same settled motion: The full-screen artwork viewer stays full-screen, with its swipeable sources, zoom and download controls. Its closing artwork spring now uses the same settled motion as the opening reveal for a more coherent return to the poster.
- Live title details and smoother page motion: The detail page refreshes AniList data while it stays open, keeping cached information visible and refreshing at most once per minute. Opening and closing share a settled scale-and-rise transition, and Info sections arrive with a tighter, lighter stagger. Version remains 2.3.9.
